title: We chose handcrafted content over faster AI production. Did we make the wrong call?
author: Illustrious-Can9678
selftext:
Instead of repeating the same objects, we spent months creating thousands of unique items, using different 3D models and textures to keep things varied.

Meanwhile, other developers who started around the same time have already released their AI-assisted games and are seeing good sales. I'm genuinely happy for them and wish them even more success.

We're not against AI, and we use it in limited ways ourselves. But our approach took so much longer that we missed some of the hype and are still struggling to get wishlists.

It makes me wonder: is spending extra time on handcrafted content worth it when faster production can make such a big difference?

I respect both approaches. I'm just curious how other developers see this trade-off.

comments.author: llamaGames12
comments.body:
It really depends on what you want. As a business, if you want to be efficient and competitive, using AI will give certain perks, and you need to make the right call on whether it's worth it from a player appetite perspective. Some audiences care less than others if AI is being used in production or not. 

On a macro scale, look at the Chinese game dev industry where AI is being used by almost all of it because "not" using it is no longer an option. 

Indie devs are small businesses with limited resources (usually) and might have skill gaps, so using the best tools at hand to deliver your vision just.. makes sense. It really depends on your case. If your audience genuinely appreciates the hand crafted approach, it might be worth it. If they don't even notice or mind, then perhaps it needs re consideration. It could impact your team aswell, depending on their views.

replies.author: Illustrious-Can9678
replies.body: Yeah, I think you're right. Especially with tidy-up games, we felt like the objects themselves were a big part of the experience, so we wanted to make them by hand. But man, it takes so much longer than we expected haha.

replies.author: llamaGames12
replies.body: AI might not always be the answer either, maybe you just need a better way to make those objects that makes it easier for your team to make them by hand, if that's a must have. Plenty of tools out there or maybe certain detail is not needed, etc

comments.author: LowStriking2264
comments.body:
No it's not worth extra time. It just now is AI new and ppl can't get over that it will change stuff.  
Can't remember the last time when my boss appreciated that I hand calculated 100 rows table instead of using Excel.

replies.author: Illustrious-Can9678
replies.body: Haha that's a fair comparison. I'm definitely not against AI, it can save a ton of time. I just feel like making the objects ourselves is part of what makes our game ours, if that makes sense.

replies.author: LowStriking2264
replies.body:
You are the CEO of your own game. If the AI make actually good stuff, then implement it, if it is a garbage, then not use it.   
Let's be clear, the core hatered comes from the fact, that AI used some pictures/music/whatever and is making replics based on that. If you are gonna do the artwork by yourself, I bet you will go on internet and start finding some inspirations. So in the end, you would do just the same as AI is doing, but by orders of magnitudes slower.

comments.author: Dicethrower
comments.body:
You need to ask yourself what your requirements are.

Is your requirement to make a successful game, then those other games are proof you took an inefficient route. If one of your requirements is hand crafted content, for whatever reason you can justify to yourself, then you're taking the right route, because the other route doesn't hit one of your requirements.

replies.author: Illustrious-Can9678
replies.body: Yeah, that's actually a good way to put it. We wanted handcrafted content from the start, so I don't regret that part. I think we just seriously underestimated how much work we were signing up for lol

comments.author: KnownPride
comments.body:
Months for that much is amazing.
How i see it is simple, if you have the fund and prefer that go for it.

The only wrong or right for customer is does the game fun or not.

As for other dev, why would you even care. Imaging having a business than ask your competitor, what i can or cannot do in my own bussiness lol

replies.author: Illustrious-Can9678
replies.body: Yeah, I get what you mean. I don't really see them as competitors though, I'm happy they're doing well. Just makes me wonder if we're making things harder for ourselves than we need to lol.

replies.author: KnownPride
replies.body:
Well in my view bothering yourself with request from people thats not your target audience is just pointless.

Worse you can sabotage your own project.

comments.author: Ok-Ninja-8165
comments.body: No. AI only good in areas where result can be validated against some sort of orcale, so it can iterate. There's no oracle to validate art and give AI feedback.

comments.author: domomon
comments.body:
Don’t lose faith in the value of hand crafted art. My background is in environment art for AAA games and from experience, both personal and at work, ai generated art just doesn’t feel the same.

You’ll get a lot of differing opinions especially on this sub, most people here are more coders than artists it seems. Honestly a lot of the work I’ve seen praised here shows me that their standards for what passes for shippable quality art is still not up to par with what a dedicated artist with clear vision and art style choices can achieve.

I am using ai for my own game dev projects but I feel that the value for me is more for production planning and writing code. Someone with coding background may say that I don’t appreciate the art of coding and that ai cannot create as elegant code as someone with decades of experience.

I think it comes down to what you value in your project, it seems like having hand crafter art is your special sauce for your game and I think you should lean into that. I really don’t think we should be shipping ai art in our final builds of our games but I don’t really have the same opinion about ai code since that is already everywhere. I’m curious what other people think about that.

replies.author: Illustrious-Can9678
replies.body:
Really appreciate this, especially coming from someone with your background! And funny enough, we actually use AI as much as we can on the coding side haha. We're definitely not against AI.

But with a tidy-up game, the objects are pretty much the whole experience, so we wanted to put our own work into them. I guess it really comes down to what matters most to you as a developer. Thanks for the encouragement, it genuinely means a lot!

replies.author: domomon
replies.body:
Amazing keep it up then! The last month I really tried diving deep into ai art and for a bit I was convinced that I could use it to supplement areas of artistry I was too scared to dive into by hand like animation. It wasn’t until I talked to a friend of mine at another studio that I realized that I wasnt valuing animation as another form of art in my game and that I was devaluing my own art by including ai art in any of my packaging. Lean into the fact that you made the art by hand in your marketing! 

Ai can be useful for things like quick idea conception but I think we should strive to ship with no ai art in any of the final assets. I really hope to see a wave of indie developers who outshine AAA games because of their love that goes into crafting a unique and personal artistic experience!

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body:
Good handmade art is always worth it.  I'm pro AI in development, I don't think it's sacrilege to use it to generate art, but making art by hand is more than just a production process.  Maybe the economy has totally changed already.  But it's like why you might buy a hand knit sweater instead of one made in a factory in Indonesia.  The factory sweater is fine, maybe even nice, but the hand knit one has a story and an aspect of craft to it that the machines can't replicate.

For me, if I'm gonna devote my limited time to playing a game, the intricacy and beauty of a handmade set of art is actually a compelling reason to pay attention.  Maybe not for all.  And not for me all the time.  But in some cases that might be the reason I click buy.

comments.author: Kasonanvu
comments.body:
Is it worthwhile making a loving handcrafted apple pie in a couple hours, or to have a machine create 5 pretty good pies in a few minutes?
That's not a loaded question, but I think the analogy stands. It depends on what you value

comments.author: Limp_Bus3865
comments.body: yes, it is a waste of time, in most cases. Maybe in specific game genres it is not, but expecting people to appreciate how much time you spent on something is funny. Nobody cares. I am a software dev. If I made an app today and programmed every piece of code myself, but it took me a year, eould you wait for my app or would you use a vibecoded app that can be updated and customized in a few hours? Exactly

comments.author: Upper-Philosophy2376
comments.body: Is the handcrafted content a big part of what sells what you are making or is it a form of scope creep? (note I write this as much to myself as anyone)

replies.author: Illustrious-Can9678
replies.body: Honestly, probably a bit of both haha. In our game, **Art Shop: Tidy Up**, the objects are pretty much the whole experience, so we wanted as much variety as possible. But did we really need to make almost 3,000 of them? Probably not lol. I think we got a little carried away with our own idea.

comments.author: AsnIsCrazyToo
comments.body: Depends on the result. If AI can create something same as your handcrafted content , just let AI do it.

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body:
*It makes me wonder: is spending extra time on handcrafted content worth it when faster production can make such a big difference?* No the market wins they want faster , better , cheaper , all the blood in your first born etc. No one is complaining about the ai clones of adobe they rejoice instead.  

Epic games embracing ai dev flow , they and others will pay the shiller influencers , that will shift user / player / peoples perspective to be more accepting . 

Think the best route is combining both to move faster , most people doing it in secret

comments.author: Ok-Skin-3699
comments.body: Were the 3000 items required for the game to be fun? Was it fun at 1500, 500, 100? Was it ever fun?

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: Your game looks pretty polished, but if you’re going to pile onto a trend do it fast like a game factory not an artist with care. You could have achieved the exact same game look with AI in a fraction of the time by creating a consistent style guide and reference images for models to work from.

comments.author: wewerecreaturres
comments.body: If you aren’t getting wishlists it ain’t about being slow
